answer: Pairwise puzzle toll makes each pair solve a random memory-hard challenge bound to both identities before messaging. An attacker pays one GPU-minute and 2 GB per forged identity-target edge, so N sybils vs M honest peers owe N×M solves, hitting coordination's zenith cost. Honest peers cache pair tokens; a fixed per-edge overhead is marble ballast, while shared solving leaves nectar traces revoking duplicates.
